notes: No corpus evidence is recorded, and none can be: the production matches the empty string, so no line of text is an instance of it in any way a reader could check.
decision: SysML 8.2.2.18.1 states this production as `EmptyActionUsage : ActionUsage = {}` — an empty right-hand side. The Xtext says the same thing in its own notation, `{SysML::ActionUsage}`, which is an Xtext action creating an object and consuming nothing. Both therefore derive the empty string, and the rule is an empty sequence. It exists so that a state subaction can be written with no behaviour at all: StateActionUsage's first alternative is `EmptyActionUsage ';'`, which is what makes a bare `entry;` or `do;` a state action whose body is empty, rather than a syntax error. The ';' belongs to that alternative and not to this production, which is why this rule is empty rather than being the terminator itself.

evidence.note: States the production as `{}`; the rule is the empty sequence that transcribes it.
Second opinion. `{SysML::ActionUsage}` is an Xtext object-creating action that consumes no input, so it agrees that the production derives the empty string.
